title: Resolve the trace root so the affected-map test passes under a symlinked TMPDIR
lead: `test_Record_TwoTests_MapsEachTestAndSelectsTheLinesItRan` fails every time on macOS with the default `TMPDIR`. `_TracingResult._relative` resolves the traced filename but compares it against an unresolved `root`. Resolve `root` once in `__init__`.
findings_note: efficiency review 2026-10-04: test_affected fails on macOS with the default TMPDIR because /var is a symlink to /private/var
boundary: **Not in this slice:** adding a macOS job to CI (an owner decision about CI minutes); changing how `record` or `select` choose tests; the suite's run time (s182 covers how to run it).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Reproduced on 2026-10-04 on macOS with Python 3.14.8. `TMPDIR=/var/folders/.../T/` and `tempfile.mkdtemp()` returns `/var/folders/...`, which `os.path.realpath` turns into `/private/var/folders/...`. The test writes its sample module under that temp directory and passes the unresolved path as `root` (`tests/test_affected.py:61-82`). `_TracingResult.__init__` stores `root` as given (`tests/affected.py:223`). `_relative` calls `path.resolve().relative_to(self.root)` (`tests/affected.py:251`), which raises `ValueError` for every traced line. So `traced` is empty and `assertTrue(only_a)` fails with `AssertionError: set() is not true`.

The test fails 3 runs out of 3 with `-k test_affected`, and passes with `TMPDIR="$PWD/.venv/test-tmp"`. The full suite passed under that TMPDIR (1081 tests, 1 skipped). One earlier full run under the default TMPDIR had a second failure whose name was not captured. Re-run the whole suite under the default TMPDIR as part of this slice and fix or file anything else. CI runs only on Linux (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so it can't see either failure. Agents developing on macOS get a red suite they have to diagnose, which is wasted tokens. This review lost several tool calls to it.

S129 made the suite independent of where TMPDIR points. This is the same class of bug, reintroduced by the affected-map tracer.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `tests/affected.py`: `_TracingResult.__init__` (`:221-225`).
- `tests/test_affected.py`: a regression test.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: only if the project logs test-only fixes (look at previous entries for test fixes; S129 is a precedent). Otherwise skip it.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_Record_SymlinkedRoot_StillMapsLines` in `tests/test_affected.py`: make a real directory `real` and a symlink `link -> real` inside a `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory. Load the sample module through `link`, call `affected.trace_suite(suite, link)`, and assert that the traced lines for `test_a` are non-empty and start with `src/slicer/sample.py:`. Skip it with `unittest.skipUnless(hasattr(os, "symlink"))` where symlinks are unavailable. This fails on Linux too before the fix, so CI covers it from then on.
2. The existing `test_Record_TwoTests_MapsEachTestAndSelectsTheLinesItRan` passes on macOS with the default TMPDIR.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: In `_TracingResult.__init__`, set `self.root = root.resolve()`. Wrap it in `try` / `except OSError` and fall back to `root` as given, which matches the defensive style of `_relative`. Change nothing else in `_relative`. Then run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` under the default macOS TMPDIR, not `.venv/test-tmp`. If any other test fails, fix it in this slice when the cause is the same symlink class. Otherwise file it with `slicer add` and the details.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` with the default TMPDIR, the same with `TMPDIR="$PWD/.venv/test-tmp"`, then `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check` and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap.
